passages.text: Eugenia pyriformis is a plant of the family Myrtaceae found primarily in Brazil. It reaches {{convert|6|to|13|m|ft}} in height and {{convert|30|to|50|cm|ft}} in trunk diameter. It is a native species of Brazil, occurring primarily in the states of Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina and São Paulo.

Cultivation
It may grow at elevations of between {{convert|300|and|1500|m|ft}}. It requires a well drained, preferably slightly acid soil.

Fruit
Eugenia pyriformis flowers between the months of August and December, and produces fruit between September and January. The yellow fruit of the plant is called uvalha and is edible. Some environmentalists have recommended use of the plant for projects of reforestation in Brazil, especially in degraded areas and permanent nature preserves.{{citation needed|date=January 2008}} The plant is also popular for ornamental or domestic purposes.
